info.title: TheraGraph
info.description:
**TheraGraph** is an evidence-grounded computational drug-discovery workbench.

It takes a researcher from a disease to prioritised compounds through retrieved public
evidence and versioned molecular models, and it keeps the two apart:

* **Retrieved facts** come from Open Targets, ChEMBL, PubChem and Europe PMC. Every
  record carries its source, source identifier, retrieval timestamp and dataset
  version, and any score shown is the score the source published.
* **Model predictions** come from TheraGraph's own models. Every prediction carries its
  model version, uncertainty, calibrated confidence and applicability-domain status, and
  is labelled as a prediction wherever it appears.

Nothing here validates a target or a drug. Candidate prioritisation orders compounds for
experimental follow-up, with the contribution of every factor shown.

### Conventions

* Errors share one envelope with a stable `error.code`.
* Expensive operations (ingestion, training, research runs) return a job or run id to
  poll.
* `X-Request-ID` is echoed on every response and appears in the structured logs.

Check every dependency needed to serve a request.

The cache is reported but not required: it degrades to cache-miss, so a Redis
outage should not remove the API from the load balancer.

Score compounds and/or raw SMILES across one or more endpoints.

Results carry uncertainty, calibrated confidence and applicability-domain status.
Anything outside the training chemistry is flagged rather than quietly returned as
equivalent to an in-domain prediction.

post.description:
Create a reproducible research run and execute it.

By default the run is enqueued and the response returns immediately with a run id
to poll: a full workflow takes tens of seconds and spends model tokens, which does
not belong in a request/response cycle.

post.description:
Enqueue a training run.

Training takes minutes (a GNN with cross-validation can take much longer), so it is
always a background job. The resulting models, evaluations and experiment are
queryable through ``/models`` and ``/experiments``.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Workflow knobs: disease, target, n_targets, min_pchembl, max_candidates, ranking_preset, allow_ingestion.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Re-submitting the same key returns the original run instead of a new one.

execute_inline.title: Execute Inline
execute_inline.description: Run synchronously and return the result. Only for small workloads; the default enqueues a background job.

idempotent_hit.title: Idempotent Hit
idempotent_hit.description: True when an identical job already existed and was returned instead.

JobAccepted.title: JobAccepted
JobAccepted.description: Returned by endpoints that enqueue background work.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.description: Endpoints to predict. Empty means every active endpoint.

model_pins.title: Model Pins
model_pins.description: Pin a specific model per endpoint, e.g. {'solubility': 'solubility-gin@2026.09.18.ab12cd34'}.

persist.title: Persist
persist.description: Persist predictions for compounds in the corpus.

weights.title: Weights
weights.description: Override objective weights by key; others keep their preset value.

include_similar_to.title: Include Similar To
include_similar_to.description: Also consider structural neighbours of this molecule.

allow_version_drift.title: Allow Version Drift
allow_version_drift.description: Permit replay when the pinned dataset or model versions have changed. The drift is recorded on the new run.
